title: The NHL Is Releasing Its Own ‘Hot’ Fanfic. Romance Lovers Hate It
gist: The NHL's 'Hot for Hockey' campaign releases 60-90 second romance-style audio stories about players on audiobook platforms and uses BookTok creators for promotion, riding the Heated Rivalry hockey-romance boom. Prominent romance authors and underrepresented fans have attacked it as pandering, citing Pride Night cutbacks, player harassment risk and AI-looking art.

insights.claim: The NHL is releasing 60 to 90 second romance-inspired audio stories starring players on audiobook platforms and will use BookTok creators to promote them, explicitly to turn romance readers into game viewers.
insights.speaker: Kate Taylor
insights.so_what: Leagues are chasing female and fandom-driven audiences through creator-led content, a growing sports-media monetisation angle.

insights.claim: Hockey romance went mainstream through the romance-novel-turned-streaming-series Heated Rivalry, followed by Off Campus, after the New York Public Library first flagged the trend in 2019.
insights.speaker: Kate Taylor
insights.so_what: Streaming adaptations of niche book genres can create new sports fan funnels and licensing opportunities.

insights.claim: The NHL calls the campaign a 'playful nod' to the cultural zeitgeist and says players approved all content, which will be exclusively focused on hockey.
insights.speaker: Jon Weinstein, NHL spokesperson
insights.so_what: League-approved player likeness use is a template other leagues may copy for engagement marketing.
insights.quote: playful nod to something that’s clearly going on in the cultural zeitgeist
insights.locator: Jon Weinstein, a spokesperson for the NHL

insights.claim: Best-selling hockey romance novelist Emily Rath refused the NHL's offer, saying it mocks the genre and uses authors' credibility to launder a tarnished brand, and alleged the slide deck included AI cover renders.
insights.speaker: Emily Rath
insights.so_what: Creator refusals plus AI-art allegations show authenticity risk when brands co-opt fan communities.
insights.quote: And they’re using popular authors and our credibility to launder their tarnished brand and lure in our readers.

insights.claim: Fans argue the NHL is courting Heated Rivalry audiences while Dallas became the first team in five years to skip a Pride Night and the league banned specialty-themed jerseys in June 2023, undermining credibility with LGBTQ fans.
insights.speaker: Lacey Conine
insights.so_what: Mismatch between marketing to diverse audiences and league policy is a reputational and sponsor-risk issue.
insights.quote: They're trying to bring in Heated Rivalry fans—and then canceling Pride Nights. That tells you where they're at.
insights.locator: “I think that they see dollar signs,”

insights.claim: Female fans say romanticised player narratives clash with Hockey Canada's 2022-reported use of registration fees to cover sexual assault claims and the NHL eligibility of five acquitted former junior players, three of whom currently play.
insights.speaker: Kate Taylor
insights.so_what: Governance and assault controversies raise tail reputation risk for leagues' marketing and sponsors.

insights.claim: Romance-driven team social content has previously triggered harassment, such as the Seattle Kraken's Alexander Wennberg and wife reporting predatory comments in 2023 after BookTok-targeted posts.
insights.speaker: Kate Taylor
insights.so_what: Player-likeness sexualisation creates duty-of-care and union exposure for leagues.

insights.claim: The campaign amounts to league-approved real-person fiction, and as marketing encourages personal connection with players, the line between fan RPF and official marketing blurs.
insights.speaker: Jess Rauchberg, University of Leeds
insights.so_what: Parasocial marketing deepens engagement but undermines fan-space norms, a monetisation versus authenticity tradeoff.

insights.claim: Critics say the campaign reinforces the idea that women only care about hockey if packaged as romance, rather than engaging with their actual concerns about the sport.
insights.speaker: Emily Rath
insights.so_what: Audience-expansion tactics that stereotype target demographics risk low conversion into game viewership.
insights.quote: They’re just encouraging the idea that women only care about hockey if it’s packaged like a romance novel
